Our story & founders

Good businessesdeserve to beunderstood.

Why we are building Tivoro

Every business
has a story.

We help yours find its place online.

Behind every business is someone building something that matters—a service, a product, a livelihood, or an idea they believe in. We believe that effort deserves a digital presence that reflects its value.

Today, customers often meet a business online before they meet the people behind it. They explore its website, understand its services, look for evidence, and decide whether to take the next step. A clear, thoughtful online presence can help turn that first introduction into trust—and trust into an enquiry, a booking, or a purchase.

We are building Tivoro to make that journey easier.

We bring business understanding, product design, and development together to help businesses establish themselves online. From a first website to a custom digital product, we shape each project around the people it serves and the problem it needs to solve.

Our work includes websites that explain businesses clearly, digital products that make services easier to use, and practical tools that simplify everyday operations. With Google Analytics and meaningful measurement, we help businesses understand how people interact with what we build and where the experience can improve.

Our approach starts with a conversation: What are you building? Who are your customers? What should become easier for them?

Those answers guide the design, the technology, and the next step.

Our ambition is to make going digital feel achievable for more businesses—from local enterprises taking their first step online to founders bringing a new product to life.

Tivoro exists to help good businesses become easier to discover, easier to understand, and easier to choose.

Tivoro — Where Ideas Become Reality.

The founders

Different strengths.
A shared way of thinking.

Co-founder / 01

Vinay Sharma

Business understanding, product strategy, and customer experience.

Vinay’s focus is on understanding the business behind a project: the people it serves, the problem it solves and the experience customers should have. That understanding helps shape the scope, product direction and next step.

Co-founder / 02

Sukhjeevan Singh

Engineering, cloud infrastructure, and reliable development.

Sukhjeevan’s focus is on the engineering behind the experience: thoughtful implementation, the supporting infrastructure and a dependable foundation for the product or website.

Co-founder / 03

Prakhar Goel

Digital products, intelligent tools, and practical AI applications.

Prakhar’s focus is on useful digital products and tools. He explores where intelligent systems and practical AI applications can simplify a task or make a service easier to use.

Make going digital
feel achievable.

From local enterprises taking their first step online to founders bringing a new product to life, we want more businesses to feel confident about what comes next.

Privacy

How your details are handled.

Updated 19 October 2026 · Website preview

Project enquiries

When you send the contact form, Tivoro stores your name, email address, organisation if provided, selected service and project message in a private enquiry database. We use these details to understand the project, reply and manage the conversation. Please avoid including sensitive personal information in your message.

Who can access an enquiry

The enquiry inbox is restricted to the authorised Site owner through sign-in and server-side access checks. Enquiries are not published on the website. If team email alerts are connected, a copy may also be sent to tivorosupport@gmail.com through the configured email service.

Security and spam protection

The form uses a short-lived, secure session cookie and a signed form token. Temporary, keyed hashes help limit repeated submissions; raw network addresses are not saved in the enquiry database. The security cookie lasts up to one hour and is not used for advertising.

Email drafts and copied briefs

If you choose “Open an email draft” or “Copy project brief”, that option prepares the details in your email app or clipboard. You decide whether to send them. Those options do not submit the project form to the enquiry database.

Keeping and removing information

Enquiries remain in the private inbox until Tivoro removes them. Archiving an enquiry keeps it in the inbox; it does not delete the details. Contact Tivoro to ask about your enquiry or request correction or removal where appropriate.

Analytics

This preview does not include advertising trackers or Google Analytics reporting. The Tools & Analytics page contains an illustrative planning example rather than client performance data.

Contact

For questions about your information, email tivorosupport@gmail.com.

Discussing a project

This website introduces Tivoro’s services and work. An enquiry starts a conversation. Project scope, fees, timing, responsibilities, handover and any support are agreed separately before work begins.

Examples and portfolio

Portfolio screenshots show selected website work. Product and analytics illustrations are labelled as concepts or planning examples. A customer goal describes the intended journey; it is not a measured performance result or a promise of a particular business outcome.

Sending an enquiry

A successful contact-form submission saves your enquiry and shows a reference number. This starts a project conversation; it does not create a booking or confirm a project agreement. External websites

Client websites, email applications and WhatsApp are independent services. Follow their own terms when using them. Contact Tivoro if a portfolio link is unavailable or you have a question about the work shown.

A few useful answers

Before we
begin.

Do you redesign existing websites?

Yes. We start by understanding what works, what feels unclear and what customers need from the experience.

Can the website include enquiries or bookings?

We can plan forms and booking journeys around your process and agree how requests reach your team.

Who provides the content?

We agree this at the start. Your knowledge of the business guides the copy, imagery and information visitors need.

What happens after launch?

We agree any ongoing support, maintenance and updates as part of the project scope.
